reason: Obcolumnar achenes and seeds are column-like but narrow at the attached base and wider above. PATO_0002347 obconical (narrow end at the base) is the nearest existing shape. PATO_0002063 columnar would lose the reversed orientation, and a new term is not justified for 3 statements.

On a perianth or involucre, polyphyllous means made of separate leaves or segments (the opposite of gamophyllous), which is FLOPO free. On a stem or plant it means many-leaved, which is not free. Single bracts are not a whorl, so they are left out.
Same as the earlier rules for pink-tinged (R0139), purple tinged (R0666) and tinged brown (R0991): the colour named is the value, and 'tinged' is a degree cue (pattern 01).

Spine-shaped describes a part's outline: narrow, stiff and tapering to a sharp point, which is subulate (awl-shaped, needle-like). PATO spiny means bearing spines, a surface quality, so the first check's alternative is wrong. Acicular is mapped to subulate the same way (C200).

In ferns an unprotected sorus has no indusium (exindusiate), so 'indusium absent' is right there. For buds or ovules 'unprotected' is a relation to another part and must not produce 'indusium absent'.

'Calyx valvular' means the lobes meet edge to edge in bud, which is FLOPO valvate (defined for perianth parts in bud). On fruits, 'valvular' refers to the part fruit valve, not to this arrangement, so fruits are excluded.

A caudex is a swollen storage stem base, and caudex is a PO synonym of stem, so 'tuberous' on the stem fits the FLOPO definition (thickened and swollen like a tuber). The stipule row is a misreading of 'cauducous' (caducous) and must not match.

'Partially' is a degree word about how far the parts are fused. The precedent 'fused to apex' -> connate (R1534) also keeps the extent in the source words. Fusion to a part of another kind would be adnate, but the word alone does not say that.
'Flushed' means tinged. The precedents rose-flushed -> pink (R1794) and flushed red -> red (R1756) map to the plain colour.
This is a faint red over the ground colour. It is handled like red tinged and suffused with red -> red (R1419): the colour is the value and the tinge is a pattern 01 cue.
The precedents narrow-ovate (R0418) and long-ovate (R0479) map to FLOPO ovate. 'Narrow' is a degree of the length-to-width ratio, which pattern 11 handles.
This is the same reading as 'suffused with purple' -> purple (R1800) and purple tinged (R0666). The wash is only a degree.
'Irregularly' only weakens the shape. The precedents irregularly rectangular (R0386) and irregularly long-rhomboidal (R1924) keep the base shape with an approximate cue.
'Offensive' means foetid only when it describes a smell. The rule must not fire for other uses of the word.

'Stems remotely branched' puts distance between the branches, not on the stem. A quality rule cannot move the bearer to the branches (only part-name rules move it), so this rule would label the stem 'distant', which is wrong.
'Weakly' is a degree word. The precedent loosely adherent -> adherent (R1771) does the same, and the other part named goes to pattern 09.
If a part does not even have a reddish cast, it is not red. The negation of PATO red is therefore true. The first check's objection (the part could still be red) does not hold.
Same as 'densely leaved' -> FLOPO leafy (R0459). 'Densely' is a degree word and was dropped there too.

The size belongs to the lumen, not to the cell or leaf that the statement describes. Quality rules cannot move the bearer (only part-name rules move it), so this would wrongly make the cell 'increased size'. It needs a lumen bearer rule instead.
Microphyllous branches have small leaves. The size belongs to the leaves, but the rule would put 'decreased size' on the branch or plant. A quality rule cannot move the bearer.
Same word as basi-dorsifixed -> dorsifixed (R2056), which is already accepted. The anther is attached by its back, and the basal position is a detail inside dorsifixed.
Caducous maps to deciduous (generic). 'Late' is timing, a degree or stage cue, handled like long-persistent -> non-deciduous (R0816).

Intrusive parietal placentas stick out from the ovary wall into the cavity. That is protruding (out past the wall surface), not its opposite. The cavity can be stated with PATO_0001645 protruding into.
FLOPO equal is the size quality of a set of like parts. It is already the target of 'equal in length' (R0163), 'equally long' (R1512) and 'equal-length' (R1165).

A bare 'thickening' does not say which way the part thickens ('towards the base' would contradict clavate), and it is often a noun ('a thickening'). Increased thickness (synonym thickened) is true in every case, as with 'weakly thickened' (R1400).
'Without margin' does not reliably mean 'not winged'. There is no usable 'margin' part class (it was rejected as a generic part), and 'not winged' is a guess, so it is better left unannotated.
'Multi-' only intensifies lacerate. The precedents lacerated (R0263) and irregularly lacerate (R1606) map to the same class.
The hairs are puberulent, short and dense enough to feel velvety. The velvety feel is a degree of the same indumentum, so puberulous is the firm value.

On a flower head, sunflower-like means ray flowers round a disc, which is FLOPO radiate. That class is defined for capitula, as the bearer constraint on 'not radiate' (R1615) shows. On other parts it means only a general look.
Crested does not mean exactly one crest. Like bigeniculate -> bent (R0516), the count stays in the source text because a crest is not a counted part.
